safety_lead_time.comparison_action: Reduce SAP safety lead time from 3.0 to 1.80 days

narrative: Material PL1__M963275D exhibits erratic but continuous demand (CV=0.328, 100% non-zero days) averaging 588.6 units/day with no detectable trend over the observed horizon (Mar 2025–Mar 2026). Lead times are short (mean 1.62 days) but unstable (CV=0.624), with one extreme outlier (19.17 days) excluded. The (r,Q) continuous-review policy is recommended with a reorder point of 2,016 units and a capacity-constrained order quantity of 3,296 units, delivering projected annual savings of $14,354 (81.8%) versus the current SAP baseline.
warnings: Order quantity reduced from unconstrained EOQ 6428 to 3296 due to max_storage_units=4357.61 constraint (SS=1061, remaining=3296).
Storage utilisation is 99.99% — any safety stock increase will breach capacity.
1 extreme lead time outlier excluded (19.17 days, >mean+4σ threshold).

research_insights.selection_rationale: Demand is erratic but continuous (CV=0.33, zero-demand fraction=0%), making continuous review superior to periodic review. The fixed EOQ-derived order quantity minimises total annual inventory cost. MOQ=421 is well below the EOQ, so MOQ does not constrain the policy.
research_insights.boundary_risk: Storage cap binds tightly (4,357 of 4,357.61 units used = 99.99%). Any upward revision of safety stock or supplier lead time increase will breach capacity. A warehouse capacity review is recommended before relaxing service level targets upward.
